commentary_title: Steady demand for LR1 in week 2
commentary_summary: The vessel utilisation was 91% in week 2, increasing approximately by 2% from the previous week. | The %laden in the East started significantly higher than it did in 2023, however, it was lower YoY in the West. Ports in the West seem to be busier than their counterparts in the East. | While the week had fairly softer trade, some disparity in rates towards the East and the West can be seen due to the situation in the Red Sea. Fresh cargoes from Asia could see rates firming next week while trade activity towards the West is likely to show improvement in week 3.

commentary_title: Disruption in the Red Sea firms up rates on most major routes
commentary_summary: The LR1 vessel utilisation peaked at a new high last week at 90.4% while the tonne-miles index stood at 86 points compared to 73.4 in week 4 of 2023. Disruptions in the Red Sea have caused many ships to take longer routes via the Cape of Good Hope. | The spot rate on TC5 climbed to WS378 last week as the CPP market firmed up with the %laden rising in both the East and the West. | The laden tonnage at anchor also rose in most regions in week 4 including India and China. There is likely to be increased tonnage headed towards Japan in week 5 while more vessels are likely to be in transit next week easing up ports especially towards the East of Suez.

commentary_title: Weak activity in the LR1 market likely to continue next week
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index increased by almost 7 points in week 7 to end at 98.5 points. It was a quieter week in the LR1 market despite the rise in the tonne-mile index which was about 15 points higher YoY. | The global vessel speed in the East declined as tonnage enquiries were low in the previous weeks with activity in the market expected to remain on the lower side in week 8 as well. However, as markets in the Far East have started to become more active after the lull of the Lunar New Year celebrations, demand for LR1 could show an uptick from the end of the week. | Nigeria's new Dangote refinery put out its first LR1 naptha cargo in the market last week which could see LR1 demand on ex-WAF routes increasing in the long run.

commentary_title: Bright week ahead for LR1s as trade activity picks up in MEG
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index for LR1 increased to 84.4 in week 11 as fresh demand for tonnage emerged towards the West of Suez, especially for the UKC to WAF route. | Freight rates increased on most routes with large gains towards the East on the MEG-Japan route. There will likely be an increase in ballast tonnage headed towards the MEG in week 12, due to the robust rise in freight rates on TC5 which could cause tonnage supply in the UKC to contract over the week. | The ballast tonnage in China and India increased last week but would likely lower over week 12 as more tonnage heads towards the Suez. With trade activity in the CPP market expected to firm next week, freight rates will also remain supported.

commentary_title: Weak markets weigh heavy on LR1s
commentary_summary: The tonne miles index declined for the first time after rising consecutively for five weeks, ending at 92.8 points in week 15. The lull of the Easter holidays followed by Eid continued to weigh heavy on freight rates as well as rates declined on most routes. | The %laden vessels in the East saw an uptick of 2% last week, declining conversely in the West. The declining ballast speed in both the East and the West point towards more vessels waiting near the ports amid limited cargoes. | There is some hope for improvement in week 16 especially towards the Med-UKC regions if tonnage supply tightens due to fewer vessels ballasting to the region. Markets opening up after the Eid holidays could help push up rates in the region. However, market activity towards the East is likely to remain weak next week.

commentary_title: Tight tonnage supply to help support freight rates
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index fell slightly last week ending the week 78.4 points as quieter markets in the West and tight tonnage supply in the East curbed the market activity for LR1s. | Freight rates firmed last week, especially in the East where the tightening of tonnage pushed up rates amid fresh requirements towards North Asia. This is likely to continue for the next couple of weeks as freight rates continue to inch higher in tandem. | The vessel speeds declined in both the East and the West except for ballast speed in the West which showed an increase. As a result, week 20 could see some uptick in market activity in the West, keeping freight rates buoyant.

commentary_title: Tonne-mile supply rises amid growing softness in the market
commentary_summary: The Posidonia week has been followed by weakness in the product tanker market, especially in the West of Suez. Despite the overall weakness, the tonne-miles index increased to 74.8 points in week 23. | The LR1 market was subdued in the West with pressure from weakening MR and LR2 markets weighing on the tonnage demand. Next week is likely to follow similar trends in the market demand with a softening in the LR1 rates. | Market activity was more mixed towards the East which could see freight rates being steady in week 24. The tonnage underway had increased last week which will likely translate into a steadiness in the LR1 demand towards the East.

commentary_title: July likely to start off with a softening in the market
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index continued to rise for the sixth week in a row ending the week at 87.7 points. The LR1 market in week 26 leaned closer towards being soft accompanied by some correction in rates happening in the market. Despite that, the transits via the COGH continued to add miles to the voyages. | The demand for CPP towards the East in particular was weak as the laden speed showed a decline over the week. More vessels ballasted Eastward might see some improvement in trade next week as cargo lists lengthen. | The rising threat of a category 5 hurricane in the West Coast Atlantic could disrupt the trade in the coming week, pushing up rates.

commentary_title: The LR1 market braces weak demand
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne miles index showed an uptick in week 29 ending the week at 74.4 points. It was a lacklustre week for the LR1s as not enough cargo was available, especially towards the East, which resulted in the freight rates adjusting downwards on the MEG-Japan route. | Towards the Med and the UKC, there was a firming in the market for MRs and LR2s leaving LR1 with fewer trades to carry out. However, next week remains hopeful for LR1 owners as tonnage demand is likely to go up with more cargoes anticipated to join the lists which could further support the freight rates in the region. | While the global ballast speed saw a steady increase, there was a marked decline in the laden speed, which could show an upturn next week, provided that more cargoes will be entering the market. There might be some congestion towards the US Gulf leading to delays or longer transits.

commentary_title: Weak demand weighs on the LR1 market
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index declined in week 32 ending the week at 66.1 points. The tonne-miles index has been on a continuous decline and has reached the lowest point this year. Demand towards the East has been weak coupled with competition from crude tankers, the LR1 tonnage demand has continued to face an overall weakness in Q3. | towards the West, the European markets have been subdued but some firming could be seen next week towards the USG. Towards the East, however, the lack of tonnage demand has caused freight rates to moderate and will likely continue for the next few weeks.

commentary_title: Spur in product demand for winter sees LR1 demand tightening
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index continued to rise for a third consecutive week as markets have been faring better for the LRs. Overall, it was a positive week for the segment, with rates also inching higher WoW. The subtle increase in the global laden and ballast speeds also shows market enthusiasm and an increase in tonnage underway, especially towards the East. | Tonnage lists seem to be tightening as demand for LR1 increases. While the markets towards the West of Suez were mixed with some softness throughout the week, the markets towards the East were in full swing. Some tightening in tonnage also helped push up rates. The positive sentiments are likely to continue next week.

commentary_title: LR1 freight rates receive support from Eastern markets
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index declined once again and ended the week at 64.5 points. The decline however slowed down compared to the sharp dips in the previous weeks. | The markets towards the West saw subdued activity throughout the week but managed to keep rates firm. The markets in the East saw much better sentiments as many vessels found prompt tonnage. This is likely to continue in the next week as well with more vessels clearing out which could push up rates slightly. | The % laden in the East and West both saw a slight increase in week 42, with ballast vessels gaining speed. As a result, next week is likely to see an uptick in activity in both the East and the West.

commentary_title: Weak product demand weighs on LR1 freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index saw an uptick in week 44 after reaching its lowest point this year. Despite an overall weakness in the clean products market, LR1s saw some support from the UKC/Med markets. As a result, week 45 is likely to see a slight improvement in the %laden towards the West. | Market activity and tonnage demand towards the west remained muted. It was a slow week, resulting in a decline in freight rates on the MEG-Japan route. This softness is likely to prevail in week 45 as well, leaving more ballast vessels to remain in port towards the MEG. The winter demand seems to have not picked up yet which will likely keep utilisation low as well.

commentary_title: LR1 market sees a firming of freight rates
commentary_summary: It was a firmer week for the LR1 market; however, the tonne-mile index did see some softening, ending the week at 68.4 points. There was a MoM decline in the vessels at port and anchor in both the East and the West. The clean products market seems to be doing slightly better this month as we get closer to colder winter temperatures. | The weakness in tonnage supply towards the East helped rates firm up slightly; however, tonnage demand also remained stable for the week. Market conditions are likely to remain stable next week, but rates might see further firming up.

commentary_title: Some momentum in LR1 market
commentary_summary: As available tonnage for LR1 remains limited, it experienced an increase in utilisation after dropping to the lowest in the previous weeks. The utilisation reached 89%, almost closer to the last year’s level. | Last week, the earnings on the Middle East to Japan route increased, supporting the LR market. However, this support will not last long, as an increase in ballast will ease the tonnage, amid the post-Christmas lull. | The tonne-mile index, on the other hand, remained stable due to a soft week. The activity and rates are expected to pick up from January when the demand will rise.

commentary_title: Uptick in LR1 rates likely to remain firm next week
commentary_summary: The LR1 market started out soft with the tonne-miles index falling slightly to reach 77.9 points in week 2. Towards the West, markets were on the weaker side with the demand for clean tankers being generally muted. To the East of Suez on the other hand, the market activity had been gaining pace especially on the MEG to Japan route as spot rates climbed higher WoW. The demand for naphtha is likely to continue pushing up rates next week. | There was a slight drop in the tonnage underway in the East and the West. However, anchorage in the East saw an uptick. With naphtha demand bound to improve further, the tonnage underway especially towards the East is likely to rise next week while it remains firm towards the West.

commentary_title: LR1 market likely to remain sluggish
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index continued to decline in week 5 since the start of the year apart having temporarily risen in week 3. The index ended at 67.7 points as fleet utilisation has declined in the past several weeks as clean product demand remained sluggish throughout January. | The markets remained quiet in both the East and the West which pushed down freight rates further. As a result, a dearth of tonnage remains, waiting to be employed while vessel speeds also seem to have slowed down globally. Next week does not look too bright either for LR1s, freight rates are likely to weaken further.

commentary_title: Outlook for LR1s for next week remains optimistic
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index continued to rise in week 8 ending the week at 87.4 points as a slight firmness in the tonnage supply aided tanker rates especially towards the East. Towards the West, the lack of tonnage demand dampened some possible freight rate gains. | The %laden grew in both the East and the West, while the laden speeds also picked up on both sides. While market conditions remain normal, with no special force driving tonnage demand, freight rates next week are likely to follow a similar trend as in week 8.

commentary_title: Tonnage underway to increase in week 11
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index declined in week 11, ending at 93 points as more vessels were at the port while the tonnage underway declined in both the East and the West. | Market activity was strong, on the other hand, especially in the East, with firm tonnage demand on the MEG-Japan route pushing up rates. This, in turn, helped support rates in the West as tonnage supply thinned out by the end of the week. Freight rates are likely to remain stable next week while the tonnage underway increases.

commentary_title: Tonne-miles index sees firmness amid weak demand
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index increased by 5.4 points, ending the week at 96.4, increasing for the second week in a row. Despite the higher tonne-miles covered, the LR1 market did not fare so well as fewer cargoes were available in the East and the West, leading to a decline in freight rates. | The vessels in port increased by over 20% in both the East and the West. Even the global ballast and laden speeds declined last week with a slight decline in tonnage underway. Market conditions are likely to remain similar next week.

commentary_title: LR2 sees gains towards the East amid mixed activity levels
commentary_summary: It was a somewhat mixed week for the clean products market; however, the tonnes-miles increased to a new high for the year, ending the week at 103.3 points. Sentiments were weaker towards the West compared to the East, but overall, tonnage has been building up more in the West than in the previous weeks. | Towards the West, market activity started strong, but an increase in tonnage supply, even from the other segments, capped any gains on freight rates. Despite steady rates in week 14, it will likely see a decline next week. | Meanwhile, freight rates firmed up towards the East as tonnage demand remained ample. However, more ballast tonnage will be attracted next week, which will weigh on freight rates.

commentary_title: Weak tonnage demand weigs on freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index continued to rise in week 20, gaining 0.9 points over the week. The global vessel speeds saw opposite trends among ballast and laden vessels as ballast speed gained 0.2 knots while the laden speed fell by close to 1 knot over the week. | The market was rather slow towards the West due to tonnage demand being weak. Towards the East however, the freight rates increased by close to 30% over the week due to low tonnage supply amid high demand. Market conditions are likley to remain the same next week.

commentary_title: LR1 markets shows weak trends
commentary_summary: The LR1 had a somewhat underwhelming week as the market activity was soft throughout the week despite a weaker tonnage supply. The tonne-mile index declined for the second consecutive week, ending the week at 86.5 points. While vessel utilisation seems to have grown weaker WoW. | The vessels in port surged last week, especially in the West which had close to a 20% increase MoM. Vessel speeds on the other hand had mixed trends with the global ballast speeds going upwards. Market conditions are likely to remain similar next week.

commentary_title: Build up in tonnage to weaken freight rates
commentary_summary: It was a mixed week for the LR1 market as the West of Suez fared better than the East side. The demand for CPP is rising towards Europe due to the peak summer months, which have increased tonnage demand in the region. The tonne-miles index improved last week, ending at 79.4 points. While utilisation has been declining in recent weeks, an improvement will likely occur soon. | The LR1 market towards the East was quiet last week, with easing tensions in the Middle East weighing down on freight rates. However, with tonnage supply likely to build up further in the coming weeks, freight rates will likely continue to weaken.

commentary_title: Market conditions for LR1s likely to brighten next week
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index showed an uptick last week after declining in the previous weeks. | Towards the West, firm market activity in the UKC supported rates last week. The %laden vessels also increased, which is expected to keep rates firm in the next week. | Meanwhile, it was a slow week in the East for LR1s, but conditions look hopeful for next week as the strong conditions in the LR2 segment are likely to have positive spillovers for LR1s.

commentary_title: Weak tonnage demand weighs on freight rates
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index showed an uptick last week after declining in the previous weeks, ending at 87.6 points. | The vessels in ports saw a massive increase MoM, especially in the West which showed close to a 61% rise. The %laden vessels have also been declining, indicating weaker tonnage demand for LR1s in the West. | The LR1 market continues to be weak overall, and weak demand for the other segments also weighs on the rates. Freight rates are likely to remain weak next week.

commentary_title: Signs of a recovery amid weak market signals
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index declined to 92.1 points in week 41 after improving for the past few weeks. Tonnage demand remained weak throughout the week, resulting in a decline in freight rates. | The vessel speed towards the West has however seen a quiet uptick in the last, rising for both ballast and laden vessels which could see increased utilisation in the West. | The %laden vessels improved in both the East and the West, indicating a potential for small gains in freight rates in the coming weeks.

commentary_title: Positive week for the LR1 market expected to continue next week
commentary_summary: The LR1 tonne-miles index increased by around 12 points in week 44, ending at 101.6 points. It was an overall positive week for the segment in both the East and the West. | Towards the West, the ex-USG routes saw rates firm up throughout the week, while towards the East, the high tonnage demand for LR2s helped push up LR1s. | Next week, we expect market conditions to remain the same and LR1 rates to remain stable.

commentary_title: LR1 freight rates firm on tight cargo flow
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index climbed to 99.3 in week 47, accompanied by week-on-week increases in both laden and ballast speeds. | Despite subdued activity in the LR1 segment, freight rates continued to edge highe, driven primarily by date-sensitive fixing. While prompt options remain available, later-month UKC positions are increasingly limited. | The steady inflow of LR1 cargoes is generating brief periods of tightness despite adequate vessel availability. Owners remain confident pointing to limited LR supply and more cargoes competing for tonnage than ships ballasting toward the Persian Gulf. We expect this supportive momentum to persist in the near term.

commentary_title: Tonne-mile index goes down as demand weakens in the LR1 market
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index declined in Week 50, accompanied by marginal week-on-week increases in both laden and ballast speeds. | Current fleet utilisation stands at 91.9%. The proportion of eastbound voyages as a percentage of laden movements declined with a similar decrease observed in westbound voyages. | Chartering activity in the East of Suez remained limited during the week and continued weak demand is likely to put downward pressure on freight rates. In contrast, LR1 tonnage availability in the West of Suez remains tight which could support an increase in rates.

commentary_title: Change in trading status - MoM
Change in trading status - MoM
LR1 market tightens on stronger fleet absorption and rising laden activity
commentary_summary: LR1 utilisation rose to 89.2%, up by 1.7 percentage points MoM, indicating improved fleet absorption and a firmer market, while the tonne-mile index declined by 10.4% YoY at 100.1, suggesting demand remains softer than in 2025. | Fleet employment strengthened across both basins, with the share of laden vessels increasing by 4.5 percentage points MoM in the east and 2.7 percentage points in the west. Combined with a 13.7% decline in laden anchorage days, this points to improved vessel utilisation and faster vessel deployment. | Regional vessel availability remains mixed with anchored capacity rising 26.7% MoM in the west and falling 9.3% in the east, suggesting relatively tighter conditions in the east of Suez. Despite bunker prices rising by 17.9% MoM to $815/tonne, vessel speeds increased, suggesting resilient freight economics and active fleet deployment.
